Congo’s MMI Resources Unveils EcoSmart Ore Tracking Platform in Push for Transparent Mining

Lubumbashi – MMI Resources, a leading Congolese mining technology provider, announced the launch of its new EcoSmart Ore Tracking platform on Thursday, signaling a step forward for digital transparency in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) metals and mining sector.

The product, which combines blockchain-based traceability with real-time logistics analytics, is designed to help mining operators and exporters comply with increasingly stringent global standards for supply chain transparency. MMI Resources said the platform will initially be rolled out across copper and cobalt operations in Haut-Katanga and Lualaba provinces—regions that account for more than 60% of the DRC’s mining exports.

“EcoSmart is an answer to our partners’ growing demand for traceable, responsibly sourced minerals,” said MMI Resources Chief Executive Pascal Mbayo during the launch event in Lubumbashi. “With this platform, local producers have a powerful tool to demonstrate compliance and win contracts with international buyers who require full visibility over every shipment.”

The DRC, home to some of the world’s largest reserves of cobalt, copper, and tin, has faced mounting regulatory pressure from importers and end-users seeking assurances over responsible sourcing. According to the Congolese Chamber of Mines, mineral exports reached $14.2 billion in 2023, with nearly 80% destined for Asian and European markets. 

Industry analysts say digital traceability solutions like EcoSmart could help Congolese miners streamline export documentation and enhance their reputation in global markets. “This launch is a timely response to evolving industry norms,” commented Francine Kabeya, an independent mining analyst based in Kinshasa. “Efforts to digitize and secure supply chain data can make Congolese producers more competitive, especially as buyers increase scrutiny of their sourcing.”

The Congo Mining Workers Union welcomed the rollout, highlighting the potential for improved workplace safety and environmental compliance. “Digital tracking helps ensure that best practices are followed from pit to port,” said union secretary Jean-Paul Kitenge.

MMI Resources said it plans to expand EcoSmart’s coverage to gold and tantalum sites by next year, pending further stakeholder consultations.
